messages:
maya: Hi team — weird one. Passport office asked me for an insurance card scan as part of a residency check for my appointment tomorrow at 9am. Do we have guidance on what they accept?

linda_hr: Hey Maya — they usually just need a copy with your name and policy number visible. Front + back. If you don’t want to share full policy number, you can redact middle digits and leave first/last 2.

gavin: Quick addition: passport offices sometimes want a dated document. If the portal provides a PDF with issue date that’s ideal.

maya: Thanks. I only have the digital card in the benefits portal. Is that okay or do you need me to print and scan?

linda_hr: Digital is fine — they accept screenshots or PDF. For security, follow these steps: 1) download the PDF from the benefits portal, 2) open in Preview/Adobe, 3) use the redact tool to mask middle policy digits (if you prefer), 4) save as PDF and bring on phone or print.

emily: If you want us to generate a temporary proof letter we can — it includes your name, employee ID (last 4) and active coverage date. That sometimes works better than the card. Want us to create one?

maya: That would be great if it’s fast. I’m nervous about redacting correctly.

emily: We can do it. Please DM me your preferred phone number and last 4 of SSN (only for verification). I’ll attach PDF here in thread when ready.

people-ops-bot: Created ticket HR-4987 to generate temporary coverage letter for maya. ETA 45 minutes.

gavin: FYI when you show digital card at desk, open the PDF instead of screenshot if possible — sometimes scan agents zoom and crop out edges.

linda_hr: @maya also check the portal under Accounts -> ID Cards -> Download PDF. If you can’t find it, reply here and we’ll walk through screen share.

maya: Got it. Thanks everyone — will DM Emily now. :thumbsup:
